digest.component_or_area: plan-review verdict assembly and LLM observability
propositions: Repeated non-fatal LLM step failures (e.g. overlap-judge batch calls) are invisible to callers consuming the plan-review gate JSON verdict because failures are swallowed to defaults and produce no verdict-level counter, making a failed step indistinguishable from a genuinely empty result.

An empty overlap[] or other LLM output caused by all retries exhausting is byte-identical to one caused by nothing matching, so observers cannot diagnose repeated silent degradation consuming wall-clock time.
Every failed LLM call already funnels through one seam (PydanticAIRunner.run except block at runner.py:573) which records spend to JSONL but produces no in-memory failure tally for the verdict.

A new run-scoped contextvar sink mirroring review_kernel/telemetry.py records failures by _call_label at the runner seam and drains into coverage.llm_step_failures in the verdict, present only when non-empty to preserve attestation-safety of clean runs.

The failure count is observability-only: it does not alter verdict string, exit code, signature, or any swallow behavior; every non-fatal failure that reaches a produced verdict is by construction one the run survived.

coverage.llm_step_failures has shape {"total": <int>, "by_step": {<call_label>: <int>}} and is declared in plan_review_verdict.schema.json, with one-line text output added to _render_plan_review_text only when non-empty.
